title: Increase of VBR resultant force at maximal trunk flexion vs upright, standing vs sitting, per patient
subcategory: VBR force increase, flexion standing vs sitting
condition: in vivo, VBR + posterior fixator, >6 months post-op

quantity.name: resultant force increase on VBR
quantity.definition: RELATIVE: increase of the resultant VBR force at maximal trunk inclination (point B) minus the average force during upright standing (for standing flexion) or upright sitting on a stool (for sitting flexion), same day. Per patient median and range over trials; max inclination angle from Fig 3a.

source.authors: Dreischarf M, Albiol L, Zander T, Arshad R, Graichen F, Bergmann G, Schmidt H, Rohlmann A
source.sample: 5 patients (4 M, 1 F) with telemeterised VBR (WP1-WP4 at L1, WP5 at L3); 135 trials (82 standing, 53 sitting) from 37 sessions; in vivo, patients with A3 compression fracture treated with posterior internal fixator + telemeterised vertebral body replacement; only sessions >6 months post-op (up to 65 months)
source.age: WP1 62, WP2 71, WP3 69, WP4 63, WP5 66 y (at surgery)

protocol.summary: Forward flexion of the upper body while standing (hands close to legs, arms hanging) and while sitting on a stool without backrest/armrests (arms hanging laterally). Force increase = force at max inclination minus mean upright force of the same posture.
how_to_simulate: Model each patient (Table 1) upright standing and upright sitting on a stool (no backrest), arms hanging
Flex the trunk to the reported maximal inclination (standing ~53 deg, sitting ~30 deg; per-patient medians in data)
Compute resultant force at the implant level (L1, or L3 for WP5) in the flexed and the upright posture of the same position and take the difference (N)

A whole-spine MSK model outputs total segment compression at the implant level, not the implant share; compare trends/relative changes unless the model includes the VBR and posterior fixator; the key target is the larger increase standing (~330 N) than sitting (~200 N)

subject_model.implant_note: VBR replaces parts of the fractured vertebral body and the adjacent discs; posterior internal fixator remains in situ
subject_model.source: Dreischarf 2015 Table 1 (sex, age, height, body mass, BMI, fractured vertebra, fixator levels, implantation date)

protocol.notes: Load measured on a telemeterised vertebral body replacement (modified Synex, 6 load components, accuracy ~2% force / 5% moment of 3000 N / 20 Nm calibration range) that shares the load with the posterior internal fixator, residual vertebral bone and bone graft; the VBR force is NOT the total spinal load. Text: average maximal inclination 30 deg sitting vs 53 deg standing; force increase ~200 N sitting vs ~330 N standing (smaller in all five patients sitting); plateau onset ~21 deg sitting (12 deg smaller than standing); plateau in ~75% of sitting trials; resultant moments usually <4 Nm.

extraction.from: Fig 3b (force increase) and Fig 3a (max inclination); text Results
extraction.uncertainty: force increase +-6 N (1 px = 2.0 N); angles +-1 deg
extraction.check_notes: Double-check (msk_invivo lead): re-digitised independently from the rendered figure - Dreischarf 2015 Fig 2b: WP1 F_transition 448 vs 452 N, WP2 635 vs 639 N, WP4 557 vs 564 N, WP1 force at alpha_max 453 vs 460 N (within +/-8 N).

pass_rule.rule: model increase within the patient range; sign and ranking: standing increase > sitting increase
